Watch the spar. (Warning of danger.)
Watch when sailing, for the reef is slack,
or the reef leaks.
Watch the mast, for the sail is coming undone. (Understand with the strong wind.)
Watch alert, for they are roasting meat.
Watch the lightning.
Watch here, and watch there, for as it is
he will do it. (One who was giving birth said to her husband: “For you I endure these pains.”
He replied: “For that I will cut it off.” She believed it, and fearing that he
would do it, she said to those who were present there: “Watch here, and watch there, for
as it is he will do it” so that they would prevent it,
and attend to her.
Watch there, for he goes to the fair.
Eye of tomato and tooth of Guinea.
(To say large eyes and teeth; it is
from the Indies.)
There are eyes that fall in love with discharge, or pay for discharge.
There are eyes that make (sic) sorrows.
Black eyes, full of mulled wine.
Grey-eyed eyes, there are not in all
neighborhoods.
Grey-eyed eyes, dogs and cats. (It is not
a defense of the blacks.)
Eyes that saw him go, will not see him
again in France.
Eyes that saw him go, will not see him come again.
Eyes that do not see, heart does not desire,
or heart that does not desire.
Eyes that do not see, heart that does not
ache, that does not break, or that does not
weep.
Eyes, that do not dress; feet, that do not
run; to you, long tail, let the devil take you. (Complaints of the captured fox.)
Eyes that see such things and ears that hear such things. (Of pity or insults, and fierce, and threats; and such things, and sometimes it is said in jest.)
Eyes that see do not age. (It exaggerates that it is pleasing to see a variety of things.)
Green eyes in few faces they see
green.
Green eyes, dukes and kings.
Evil eyes, whoever looks at them catch
their malice or their malady.
Hatred of mortals should not be immortal.
Bag of good wine, and leaping horse, and quarrelsome man, never lasts
long with his master.
Empty bag, I call it leather. (Bag is
used in feminine: a bag and little bag,
and here the proverb made it masculine by the
consonant, and the ending e made it
capable of both genders.)
Craftsman who has no money, put
a trim on the board. (It is of tailors, and
it could say: tailor who has no money...)
Craftsman who does not lie, does not live among people.
Craftsman, what do you know how to do? Hem
and over-sew, or patch and over-
sew. (For fun they change the ending patch
and over-eat.)
Foreign craft, money costs. (In un-
derstanding it, when one by his industry does something of foreign craft, usually
friends make him give them to drink and pay the patent, as examination
of new craft that he took; and it is said
of one who meddled in craft and trade of
which he had no experience and lost
in it.)
Saddler’s craft, put in straw and
take out money.
Council’s craft, honor without profit.
Hand’s craft brothers do not divide. (That each one leaves the other
the work; there are also crafts that
one alone without others must do
by himself.)
Craft that does not sustain your life give
it dismissal.
Bartolo has a craft for the whole day.
Vain craft and with pain to the one who
follows it condemns.
Mendicant’s craft, raise the son and
then the grandson.
Base craft, whoever uses you more thrives less, or whoever uses it more.
Offer much to one who asks little.
(Species of denying everything.)
Offer much, species is to deny
